Rama. A legendary prince and an avatar of Vishnu, revered as the exemplar of righteousness and virtue in Hindu tradition.

Rama is the protagonist of the Ramayana, one of Hinduism's two great epics. He represents the ideal king and the perfect devotion to duty, even in the face of personal sacrifice. He is an avatar of Vishnu, incarnated to defeat the demon king Ravana and restore cosmic order to the world.

Born as a prince of Ayodhya, Rama embodies the virtues of a perfect son, husband, warrior, and king throughout his life's journey. The Ramayana details his exile from his kingdom, his wife Sita's abduction by Ravana, and their triumphant return.

He is accompanied by his devoted brother Lakshman and the monkey god Hanuman, forming one of literature's most celebrated relationships. Together, these three represent the bonds of loyalty, duty, and spiritual devotion. Rama is depicted with blue or golden skin, holding a bow and arrows. These symbolize his martial prowess and his readiness to defend dharma.

His reign, the Rama Rajya, becomes the Hindu ideal of perfect governance: just, peaceful, and prosperous. Though an avatar of the divine, Rama lives and struggles as a mortal. He accepts exile to honor his father's oath and maintains dharma even when it costs him dearly.

He is worshipped during Diwali, the festival of lights, which celebrates his victory over evil and his return to his kingdom. Rama's life exemplifies the Hindu principle that true greatness lies in upholding righteousness regardless of personal cost.
